summary: Iteration 2 backend testing complete for Omega Chat. All 36 pytest tests pass (21 regression from iter 1 + 15 new). New coverage: (1) ConversationView.unread_count — reflects peer messages, ignores own sends, zero when no peer msgs, resets after mark-read, increments again on new incoming; (2) POST /api/conversations/{id}/read — 401 without auth, {ok:true, updated:N} on success, only peer messages get read_at set (own stay null), idempotent (second call updates:0), 404 for non-participant; (3) GET /api/users/discover — 401 without auth, excludes self, excludes users already in a conversation, sorted by created_at DESC, <=12 results, no _id leak; (4) WS 'read' broadcast — Bob receives {event:'read', data:{conversation_id, reader_id, read_at}} when Alice marks-read; (5) WS 'typing' — broadcast to peer only, sender never gets echo, non-participant sender is silently ignored (no leak to real participants). MongoDB _id is not leaked in any of the new responses.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py mark_conversation_read broadcasts the 'read' event only when modified_count > 0. This is correct/efficient but means calling /read on an already-read conversation will not re-notify the sender. Current tests confirm the intended behavior; document if UI relies on always-broadcast.

WSManager.broadcast_to_conversation iterates 'participants' and dispatches to every uid including the actor. For messages this is desirable (sender sees their own via HTTP anyway; other devices sync). For 'read' events the sender-actor also receives their own read event — currently benign but could cause duplicate UI updates on the reader's other tabs.
typing handler swallows all exceptions with a bare 'except Exception: pass' inside the receive loop, which will hide malformed payloads. Consider logging at debug level.
server.py still uses deprecated @app.on_event startup/shutdown (from iter 1); non-blocking.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_iteration2.py (new — 15 tests: unread_count, mark-read, discover, WS read+typing)
